sections.html: Like all Macrobrachium species they need good water quality, otherwise however they are not demanding.

A shrimp aquarium should not be lit up too brightly, and/or be easily darkened with some floating plants. The roots of the floating plants offer protection to the new generation against their sometimes quite predatory parents. Further there should be a lot of hiding places; with bogwood, coconut shells and rocks, beautiful underwater landscapes can be arranged.
All usual kinds of food are eaten greedily.

Remarkable are their extremely long, name-giving “arms”, which can give the full grown animals an enormous broad reach. With that they are able to track small fish successfully, which naturally limits their use in the community tank. Together with larger fish species or in a shrimp aquarium they are however interesting animals.
In January 2006 the long arm shrimp Macrobrachium idae was imported from Sri Lanka.
